texts.title: Where did all the phone boxes go?

paragraphs.text: Not long ago, the public telephone box was one of the most familiar objects in any town. It stood on street corners, outside railway stations and post offices, and in the centre of villages too small to have a shop. For people without a telephone at home, which until the 1970s meant a large part of the population in many countries, it was the only way to call a doctor, arrange to meet a friend or speak to a relative who lived far away. Today most of those boxes have gone, and the few that remain are rarely used for their original purpose. Their story says a good deal about how quickly a piece of public equipment can move from necessity to curiosity.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The first public telephones appeared in the late nineteenth century, only a few years after the telephone itself. At first they were placed inside shops, hotels and offices, where an attendant collected the charge and connected the call by hand. Coin-operated machines, which allowed a caller to pay without help, followed in the early twentieth century, and it was these that made it possible to put a telephone outdoors. Early street kiosks were built of wood, but they were easily damaged, and most countries soon replaced them with heavier designs in cast iron or concrete, often painted in a bright colour so that they could be found quickly in an emergency.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Using a public telephone was not always simple. Callers needed the right coins, and in many places the machine had two buttons, one to press when the call was answered and another to press to get the money back if it was not. Queues formed outside popular boxes in the evenings, when calls were cheaper, and an unwritten rule limited each caller to a few minutes. Directories hung on chains inside the kiosk, although they were frequently torn or missing. For young people in particular, the phone box offered something that a telephone at home could not: a conversation that parents could not overhear. Many boxes also had a small shelf for writing down numbers and a light that came on at dusk.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The number of boxes reached its peak in most countries in the 1980s and 1990s. By then, operators were under pressure to keep every box working, since a broken telephone could leave someone unable to call for help, and maintaining thousands of kiosks exposed to the weather and to vandalism was expensive. Card-operated telephones, introduced partly to reduce theft from coin boxes, made calls more convenient but did little to make the network profitable, because the number of calls made from each box was already beginning to fall as more households installed their own lines. Some operators tried to earn extra income by selling advertising space on the outside of their kiosks.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: The arrival of the mobile phone completed the change. Within about fifteen years of mobiles becoming widely available, the number of calls made from public telephones had fallen so far that many boxes were used less than once a week. Operators began to remove them in large numbers, usually after consulting the local council, and in several countries a box can now be taken away only if nobody objects within a set period. Boxes in places with poor mobile reception, such as main roads and stretches of coast where accidents happen, were often kept for longer, since they were still the only reliable way of calling the emergency services.
paragraphs.label: E

paragraphs.text: Not everyone welcomed the removals. Older residents who had never owned a mobile, people who could not afford one and visitors whose phones did not work locally all lost a service they relied on. Campaigners argued that a public telephone should be treated like a post box, as something a community is entitled to whether or not it pays for itself. Operators replied that the money spent on rarely used boxes would be better spent on improving mobile coverage, which would benefit far more people, and that most of the remaining boxes were costing more to clean than they earned.
paragraphs.label: F

paragraphs.text: Meanwhile, some of the empty kiosks have been given a second life. Communities in many places have adopted old boxes, often for a nominal sum, and turned them into tiny libraries where people leave and take books, into information points for walkers, or into cases for defibrillators, the devices used to restart a heart that has stopped. Others have been converted into small shops selling coffee or flowers, while a number of the most attractive designs have been protected as part of the historic street scene, which means that they cannot be removed or altered without permission.
paragraphs.label: G

paragraphs.text: It would be wrong to see the public telephone simply as a victim of progress. For almost a century it gave millions of people a connection they could not otherwise have had, and some of the reasons it once mattered, such as the need for a way to call for help that does not depend on owning a device, have not entirely disappeared. The boxes that survive, whether as libraries or as protected monuments, are a reminder that public services are shaped by the technology of their time, and that when the technology changes, the question of who is left without access has to be asked again.
paragraphs.label: H

document.title: Section 3 · where the phone boxes went

topic.en: A general-interest text: how street telephone boxes appeared, why they disappeared and what has become of them.
topic.kk: Жалпы қызығушылық мәтіні: көшедегі телефон будкалары қалай пайда болды, неге жойылды және олармен не болды.
topic.ru: Текст общего интереса: как появились уличные телефонные будки, почему они исчезли и что с ними стало.

items.quote: it was these that made it possible to put a telephone outdoors

explanation.en: “it was these that made it possible to put a telephone outdoors” → i. Paragraph B: from a phone in a shop to a kiosk in the street.
explanation.kk: «it was these that made it possible to put a telephone outdoors» → i. B абзацы — дүкендегі телефоннан көшедегі будкаға дейін.
explanation.ru: «it was these that made it possible to put a telephone outdoors» → i. Абзац B — от телефона в магазине до будки на улице.

items.quote: an unwritten rule limited each caller to a few minutes

explanation.en: “an unwritten rule limited each caller to a few minutes” → ii. Paragraph C: queues, coins, directories. Cheap evening calls are a detail, not the topic (viii).
explanation.kk: «an unwritten rule limited each caller to a few minutes» → ii. C абзацы — кезек, тиын, анықтамалық. Кешкі арзан қоңырау — тақырып емес, деталь (viii).
explanation.ru: «an unwritten rule limited each caller to a few minutes» → ii. Абзац C — очереди, монеты, справочники. Дешёвые вечерние звонки — деталь, а не тема (viii).

items.quote: did little to make the network profitable
keywords: did little to make the network profitable

explanation.en: “did little to make the network profitable” → iii. Paragraph D: the boxes are costly to keep and used less and less.
explanation.kk: «did little to make the network profitable» → iii. D абзацы — будканы ұстау қымбат, ал қоңырау азая береді.
explanation.ru: «did little to make the network profitable» → iii. Абзац D — содержать будки дорого, а звонков всё меньше.

items.quote: Boxes in places with poor mobile reception, such as main roads and stretches of coast where accidents happen, were often kept for longer

explanation.en: Calls collapsed and boxes were removed in large numbers, except where reception was poor (“were often kept for longer”) → iv.
explanation.kk: Қоңырау азайды, будкалар жаппай алынды, бірақ байланыс нашар жерде қалдырылды («were often kept for longer») → iv.
explanation.ru: Звонков стало мало, будки массово убирают, но в местах без связи их оставили («were often kept for longer») → iv.

explanation.en: “Not everyone welcomed the removals” → v. Paragraph F: the case against removal. New uses (vi) belong to paragraph G.
explanation.kk: «Not everyone welcomed the removals» → v. F абзацы — алып тастауға қарсы уәждер. Будканың жаңа қолданысы (vi) — G абзацы.
explanation.ru: «Not everyone welcomed the removals» → v. Абзац F — доводы против сноса. Новые применения будок (vi) — это абзац G.

groups.instruction: The text has eight paragraphs, A–H. Choose the correct heading for paragraphs B–F from the list of headings below. Write the correct number, i–viii.

items.quote: an attendant collected the charge and connected the call by hand
items.prompt: The earliest public telephones could not be used without the help of an employee.

explanation.en: “an attendant collected the charge and connected the call by hand” → TRUE: a member of staff was needed.
explanation.kk: «an attendant collected the charge and connected the call by hand» → TRUE: қызметкерсіз қоңырау шалу мүмкін болмаған.
explanation.ru: «an attendant collected the charge and connected the call by hand» → TRUE: без служащего позвонить было нельзя.

items.quote: Early street kiosks were built of wood, but they were easily damaged
items.prompt: Early street kiosks were made of stronger materials than later ones.

explanation.en: “built of wood, but they were easily damaged” → FALSE: the first kiosks were weak and were replaced with iron or concrete.
explanation.kk: «built of wood, but they were easily damaged» → FALSE: алғашқы будкалар осал болған, кейін шойын мен бетонға ауыстырылған.
explanation.ru: «built of wood, but they were easily damaged» → FALSE: первые будки были непрочными, их заменили на чугун и бетон.

items.quote: Queues formed outside popular boxes in the evenings, when calls were cheaper
items.prompt: It cost less to make a call later in the day.

explanation.en: “in the evenings, when calls were cheaper” → TRUE: evening calls cost less.
explanation.kk: «in the evenings, when calls were cheaper» → TRUE: кешке қарай қоңырау арзанырақ болған.
explanation.ru: «in the evenings, when calls were cheaper» → TRUE: вечером звонить было дешевле.

items.prompt: Callers preferred card-operated telephones to coin machines.

explanation.en: Card phones “made calls more convenient”, but callers’ preferences are never reported → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Карталы аппарат «made calls more convenient», бірақ қоңырау шалушылар қайсысын таңдағаны айтылмаған → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Карточные автоматы «made calls more convenient», но что выбирали сами звонящие, не сказано → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: usually after consulting the local council
items.prompt: Most local councils opposed the removal of boxes in their area.

explanation.en: We learn that the council is consulted, not how councils usually responded → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Жергілікті билікпен ақылдасатыны айтылған; ол әдетте қалай жауап бергені айтылмаған → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Сказано, что с местной властью советуются; как она обычно отвечала, не сказано → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: the money spent on rarely used boxes would be better spent on improving mobile coverage
items.prompt: Operators have used the savings from removed boxes to improve mobile coverage.

explanation.en: “would be better spent” is the operators’ argument, not a report that the money was spent → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: «would be better spent» — операторлардың уәжі ғана; ақша байланысқа жұмсалғаны туралы дерек жоқ → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: «would be better spent» — это довод операторов, а не отчёт о том, что деньги потратили на связь → NOT GIVEN.

groups.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the text? Write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

items.quote: Communities in many places have adopted old boxes, often for a nominal sum

explanation.en: “Communities in many places have adopted old boxes” → communities: after “local” with no article, the plural is needed.
explanation.kk: «Communities in many places have adopted old boxes» → communities: «local» сөзінен кейін артикль жоқ, сондықтан көпше түр керек.
explanation.ru: «Communities in many places have adopted old boxes» → communities: после «local» без артикля нужно множественное число.

explanation.en: “into information points for walkers” → walkers: the box becomes an information point.
explanation.kk: «into information points for walkers» → walkers: будка жаяу серуендеушілерге ақпарат беретін орынға айналған.

items.quote: a number of the most attractive designs have been protected as part of the historic street scene
items.prompt: Some of the best-looking designs are now 14 ____

explanation.en: “the most attractive designs have been protected” → protected. “Best-looking” = “most attractive”.

explanation.ru: «the most attractive designs have been protected» → protected. «Best-looking» = «most attractive».
